newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian central bank chief sees rates lowering.
newsitem.headline: Croatian central bank chief sees rates lowering.

text.p: The head of Croatia's central bank said on Friday he expected lending rates to ease further amid overall monetary stability.

"I expect with a lot of optimism the trend towards easing of lending rates to continue," said Marko Skreb, governor of the National Bank of Croatia (NBH). "But the trend does not need to be linear," he told a meeting with commercial bank executives.
In the last nine months, inter-bank rates have fallen to 8-9 percent from 32 percent, while the rate for central bank liquidity bills sank under 10 percent from 27 percent.
At the same time January to September inflation was kept at a relatively low level of 2.4 percent, Skreb said.
He said the government's structural reforms in the banking sector, particularly the rehabilitation of Rijecka and Splitska Banka this spring, were the main factors in the improvement.
Skreb welcomed the entry of foreign banks on the domestic market, which would sharpen the competition, lower the profit margin between passive and active rates and force Croatian banks to cut costs.
Following Austria's Raiffeisen Bank and Bank Austria, Italy's Casa di Risparmio di Trieste opened in Zagreb on Friday.
Skreb said the number of banks would shrink from the current 60-plus, as some will be forced to merge to survive.

The central bank will also continue to lower the reserve requirements for commercial banks from the current 35.8 percent of kuna deposits and 40 percent of foreign currency. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
